head: 88692cf0d67aeb7aed41ae647a8524b21af374f5
label: task154-outbox-marksent-thread-wait-attribution
purpose: Read-only adjudication ONLY: without enabling/resetting any Performance Schema instrument and without any production change, can the real markSent conditional UPDATE's wait cost (or smaller fsync/lock/pure-SQL items) be safely attributed to the client connection thread that executed it, using only already-populated P_S summary tables? Counterexample-first: dedicated scratch schema task154_wait_scratch with the repository's real DDL; CONNECTION_ID() -> P_S THREAD_ID mapping; target connection executes only the verbatim production markSent SQL; observer connection takes before/after snapshots; repeated small samples plus same-thread negative controls (zero-row UPDATE, SELECT 1, same-table SELECT) and background-path checks.

reasons: Background attribution unresolved: thread/innodb/log_flusher_thread and log_writer_thread (run B also io_write/page_flush_coordinator/dblwr) have NON-zero wait increments in the same sequence window; the 2 binlog file waits counted on the client thread are only that statement's own share; the redo-flush share borne by background threads can neither be confirmed nor quantified, and the seed INSERTs in the same window travel the same commit path.

Instrumentation gap: all wait/synch/* instruments are disabled -> 'waiting for log flush completion' style sync waits are simply NOT collected; events_waits_history_long = NO -> the wait event tree (nesting/ordering) cannot be reconstructed from aggregates.
Cannot name the item: the 2 wait/io/file/sql/binlog events are only '2 waits on this file class'; they cannot be split into write/fsync, nor aggregated with redo into a 'persistence cost'.

Measurement accounting: this instance has no setup_timers table (unit empirically calibrated as picoseconds); idle is mixed in the same summary table and must be excluded; client wall clock and server statement event time are two independent observations that must not be subtracted or divided.
verdict.note: TASK-152's 0.739312 and TASK-153's batch-end-mark NO-GO were NOT modified, NOT overturned, and NOT used to infer optimizable sub-items. No percentage of fsync/lock/pure-SQL was produced.

measuredEvidence.reproducibleCombination: every row-hitting UPDATE window (12 across runs A+B incl. incrRetry) shows the same client-thread combination: wait/io/file/sql/binlog x2, wait/io/table/sql/handler x2, wait/lock/table/sql/handler x1; plus one idle (~0.22-0.26 s between windows, excluded). Zero-row UPDATE and SELECT windows do NOT produce binlog waits; SELECT 1 produces no non-idle waits at all.
measuredEvidence.globalVsThreadCounts: thread-scoped binlog events from the 7 row-hitting statements (warmup 1 + w1..w5 + n5) = 14; global sql/binlog = 24 in the same period. The difference matches other connections' commit activity (seed INSERTs) and MUST NOT be apportioned to markSent - this is the empirical proof that global counter deltas cannot be used for a single-statement measurement.

unclosedReasons: background attribution unknown: thread/innodb/log_flusher_thread, log_writer_thread (run B also io_write/page_flush_coordinator/dblwr) have non-zero increments in the same window; the 2 client-thread binlog waits are only that statement's own share; the redo-flush share borne by background threads can neither be confirmed nor quantified, and the seed INSERTs share the same commit path in the same window
instruments not covering: all wait/synch/* disabled (the actual 'wait for log flush completion' sync wait is NOT collected); events_waits_history_long = NO (no event-tree reconstruction)
cannot name: the 2 wait/io/file/sql/binlog events cannot be split into write/fsync nor merged with redo into a 'persistence cost'

accounting: no setup_timers table (unit calibrated empirically as ps); idle mixed in the summary must be excluded; client wall and server statement event are independent observations - no subtraction/division
restrictedFactualStatement: In THIS isolated environment and THIS instrument setting, a row-hitting UPDATE stably leaves, on ITS client connection thread, the directly readable combination 'binlog file wait x2 + table handler wait x2 + table lock wait x1', and zero-row UPDATE / non-target SQL do not produce that combination. This is NOT a GO, NOT an optimization authorization, and NOT a full transaction cost.
